title: forma.room.json — portfolio manifest for `forma room`
description: What makes the Control Room parametric instead of hand-cut per portfolio: another program changes only this file. `today` is a determinism anchor — room/check/room-presentable never call Date.now(); every run is pinned to the date this file names.

title.description: Control Room page title. Never inherited from model.meta.title, which describes an architecture snapshot, not the room.

theme.description: Control Room color theme. Default dark.

staleAfterDays.description: room-presentable fails if c4-issues.json.fetchedAt is older than this many days before `today`. Default 14.

linkMaxFiles.description: A commit touching more files than this is a sweep and attributes to no node (still counted, named in `tec`). Default 50.

maxBytes.description: Caps document bytes read across the portfolio so room generation stays bounded.

id.description: Stable program key used to join portfolio data without depending on a display name.

enabled.description: Default true. A program set to false stays in the manifest and out of the briefing, and the Options view names it as deliberately excluded — deleting the entry would lose that distinction, and `forma scan` never overwrites a false.

repo.description: Filesystem path to the checkout. Relative paths resolve against the manifest file's own directory so invocation location cannot change the target.

issues.description: Path to this program's c4-issues.json fact base.

model.description: Path to this program's architecture model when it participates in the room.

topology.description: Path to this program's topology overlay when one exists.

health.description: Path to this program's health overlay when one exists.

findings.description: Path to this program's findings overlay when one exists.

auditPlan.description: Offline counter-verification plan written by `room update --counter`.

counterResults.description: Agent-written counter-verification results consumed by `room update --counter`.

blockedBy.description: Declares what 'waiting on a human' means for this program; lib/ never infers it. Measured reality differs: haben uses needs-human, arbiter uses needs-human plus owner-decision, and viafera has no such label because status:parked means deliberately stopped, not waiting.

include.description: Globs selecting only git-tracked files, so generated or local files cannot silently enter the room.

canon.description: Paths carried in full, in this order, so a reading order somebody chose survives into the page. Everything else `include` selects is listed with a link but not embedded. A canon document that would exceed docs.maxBytes is listed with that as its reason, never truncated.

rtm.description: The requirements traceability matrix, opt-in by presence: a program that declares no rtm derives none and sees none of its four gate assertions. Paths are relative to the PROGRAM'S checkout, not the manifest — docs/PRD.md means that repository's PRD.

path.description: Repo-relative markdown file. Must be tracked by git, or its rows never enter the matrix and the document is named as skipped.

idPattern.description: Regex an id cell must match for its row to be a requirement, e.g. "^R-\\d+$". A column called id that does not match is a different table, not a near miss to repair.

role.description: What this document contributes to the chain: requirement, design, feasibility, verification. Free text — lib/ never enumerates one project's stages.

id.description: Header name of the id column, when it is not auto-detected.

describe.description: Header name of the text column, when it is not auto-detected.

satisfies.description: Header name of the upstream-reference column, when it is not auto-detected.

verified.description: Header name of the verification column, when it is not auto-detected.

issues.description: Header name of the issue column, when it is not auto-detected.

requireIssuesFrom.description: Document paths whose rows MUST land on GitHub issues or name a verification. A row in one of these with neither is reported uncovered and fails `forma check`. This is what makes 'the issues are the complete WBS' a falsifiable claim rather than an aspiration.

order.description: family -> values ordered most severe first, e.g. {"priority": ["P0", "P1", "P2"]}. Values not listed sort after every declared value.

exclude.description: Label families to never promote to an axis, however populated.

minPopulation.description: A family below this many labeled issues stays in the named 'other' bucket. Default 3.
